title: Carbon credit market with paid verifiers and audits
summary: Verifiers, paid a fee per report, tell the market how good each project is. Sellers and buyers then send sealed orders to a call auction per project. Afterwards some traded projects are audited: the true quality is made public and a verifier whose report was far off pays a penalty.

roles.name: verifier
roles.description: Measures the quality of its assigned projects and publishes a report on each.

roles.name: seller
roles.description: Owns one project and offers its credits.

roles.name: buyer
roles.description: Wants credits; a credit is worth more to it the higher the project's true quality.

steps.name: verification
steps.description: Each verifier sees its own noisy measurement of its projects and reports one number per project.

steps.name: market
steps.description: Sellers post an ask for their project and buyers send one optional order per project, all sealed.

steps.name: clearing
steps.description: Each project's orders clear in a uniform-price call auction.

steps.name: audit
steps.description: Each traded project is audited with a fixed probability; an audit reveals its true quality to everyone and penalizes a verifier whose report was off by more than the tolerance.

repeats.what: The four steps repeat each round with the same participants.
carries_over: Each verifier's audit record (shown to buyers only if reputation_visible is on).
Last round's public prices and volumes.

secrets.what: A project's true quality is revealed to buyers and sellers only by an audit.

payoffs.description: Value times quality of the credits bought, minus what was paid.
Revenue minus cost of the credits sold.
A fee per report, minus a penalty per audited report that was off by more than the tolerance.

invariants.name: audit_only_traded
invariants.statement: Only projects that traded in the round can be audited.

invariants.name: no_overselling
invariants.statement: A seller never sells more credits than it has.

assumptions.text: If a verifier, seller or buyer does not act, the whole run stops.
A buyer's credits are valued at the true quality if the project was audited that round, and at the reported quality otherwise (settle_on = reported).
Sellers do not see their project's true quality as a number; they see its cost and the verifier's report.
Audit results are public: every participant is told each audited project's verifier, report and true quality.
A seller is not told its profit, only its revenue.
The clearing price of a project is the midpoint between the last accepted bid and ask; ties at the margin are rationed in proportion to quantity.
